title: Finite type coherent relations on an iterated open slice
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $\mathcal G$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] in the module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $V=(W\hookrightarrow U)$ be an object of the open slice, so $W\subseteq U$ is open. For every finite set $I$ and morphism $f:((\mathcal O_X|_U)|_V)^{\oplus I}\to (\mathcal G|_U)|_V$ on the iterated slice, $\ker f$ is of finite type.

source.place: Modules, Definition 01BV (definition-coherent), condition (2), applied to W; open-restriction convention in Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (2). Verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01BV and /tag/01BY.

proof.text: Use Over.iteratedSliceEquiv V and SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence with identity ring maps to identify modules over V.left with modules over the iterated slice. The structure module and G.over V.left are identified with their iterated restrictions. Reindex the free source using freeFunctor.mapIso and the equivalence ULift(Fin(card I)) with I; mapFreeIso transports this free module through the site equivalence.

Take the preimage g of the conjugated map f under the module equivalence. Apply the relation clause hG.2 at V.left and card I to obtain finite type of kernel g. Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentKernelConditionRestriction to reuse its existing proved private finiteType_pushforward_leftAdjoint theorem, which transfers finite type through the site equivalence using finite local generators. PreservesKernel.iso and kernel.mapIso identify the transported kernel with kernel f; reuse the same imported module's finiteType_of_iso to transfer finite type along this isomorphism. No helper is restated or reproved, and no nonempty-open or positive-rank assumption is used.
